title: The meaning of belief in the Qur'an
question: When I have faith in the Noble Qur'an, what then is the ruling concerning one who denies the whole of the Qur'an Majīd, either entirely or in part, or who denies a portion of the Qur'an Sharīf, either entirely or in part — whether that denial is made with the tongue or through the other limbs?
answer:
Complete affirmation of the Qur'an Pāk is obligatory.

If, concerning the whole Qur'an or any part of it (a verse), a person holds the belief that it is not revealed from Allah Ta'ālā, then faith does not remain.

And if the deficiency is in action, then it will not be ruled disbelief. Faith itself is weakened and enfeebled by it, but it does not come to an end so long as the affirmation of the heart remains.

And Allah, glorified be He, knows best.
references: Sharḥ Fiqh al-Akbar, p. 205 (Kutub Khana Rahimiyya, Deoband)
